input.rationale: There is no indemnification clause anywhere in the Agreement. The body runs contiguously from Section 19.5 (p0075) straight to "21. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY" (p0076) with no Section 20, and searches for "indemnify", "defend" and "hold harmless" return no operative obligation — only downstream references that presuppose an indemnity: Section 9.3 relies on "the remedies required by Section 20.5", Section 19.4 preserves remedies for "indemnified claims", Section 21.3 treats "its indemnification obligations" as Excluded Claims, and Section 30.5 preserves "vested indemnity rights". The contiguous paragraph numbering confirms this is a genuine drafting gap rather than an extraction omission. This falls in walk-away territory (no Vendor IP indemnity at all) and fails both the preferred and fallback positions, so severity is critical: as drafted, Customer bears its own defence costs for third-party claims that the Services infringe IP, and has no contractual recourse for Vendor-caused data incidents or breaches of law beyond ordinary damages, which the Section 21.1 cap would then govern. We inserted a new Section 20 at the preferred position: a Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused unauthorized access to Customer Data, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, extended to Customer Affiliates; customary IP exclusions (unauthorized modification, combination, Customer specifications); a standard notice/control/cooperation procedure with a no-adverse-settlement carve-out; procure-modify-replace-refund remedies numbered 20.5 so the existing Section 9.3 cross-reference resolves correctly; and a narrow Customer indemnity confined to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law. No super-cap was added because Section 21.3 already treats indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims outside the liability cap, which is better than the fallback's 3x super-cap.

proposal.summary: Insert a new Section 20 (Indemnification) with a Vendor indemnity for IP infringement, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach and wilful misconduct, standard claim procedure, IP remedies (supporting the existing Section 20.5 cross-reference), and a narrow Customer indemnity.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no Section 20, so there is no indemnity at all even though Sections 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 assume one exists. We have inserted a Vendor indemnity covering third-party IP claims, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents and wilful misconduct, with the usual notice/control/cooperation procedure and procure-modify-replace-refund remedies that Section 9.3 already cross-references, plus a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

ops.text: Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services, Deliverables, or Vendor Technology infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to, use, or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

Vendor's obligation under Section 20.1(a) does not apply to the extent a claim arises from Customer's unauthorized modification of the Services or Deliverables, combination of the Services or Deliverables with materials not supplied or recommended by Vendor where the claim would not have arisen but for the combination, or Vendor's compliance with written specifications supplied by Customer.

Customer shall indemnify Vendor against third-party claims to the extent arising out of content or materials Customer provides for use in the Services in violation of a third party's intellectual property rights, or Customer's breach of Applicable Law. Customer has no other indemnification obligation under this Agreement.

The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of the claim, provided that delay does not excuse the indemnity except to the extent it materially prejudices the defence; permit the indemnifying Party to control the defence and settlement; and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense. The indemnifying Party shall not settle a claim in a manner that imposes a non-monetary obligation on, or admits liability or wrongdoing of, the indemnified Party without its prior written consent. The indemnified Party may participate with its own counsel at its own expense.

If a claim under Section 20.1(a) arises or is reasonably likely, Vendor shall, at its expense, procure for Customer the right to continue using the affected item, or modify or replace it with a functionally equivalent, non-infringing item. If neither remedy is commercially practicable within a reasonable period, either Party may terminate the affected item and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for it and, for a paid-up licence or accepted Deliverable, the Fees paid for it.
